scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The required features are Kcnk3 and Kcnk9, and both are accurately explained as encoding TASK-family background potassium channels whose increased resting conductance would lower input resistance. Their proposed importance across visual-cortical interneuron subclasses remains speculative but is biologically defensible and clearly framed as a testable hypothesis.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: Kcnk3 and Kcnk9 are explicitly connected through TASK-channel expression and open probability to resting potassium conductance, membrane time constant, and input resistance. HCN conductance and cell size are appropriately treated as competing determinants or covariates rather than fully integrated parts of the principal mechanism. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the focus-feature–target mechanism is explicit, biologically resolved, and includes all features required by the primary hypothesis.
